statement: The analytic germ at 0 of the finite prefix-cost aggregate determines its weighted multiplicity distribution. Classical unconditional logarithmic zeta zero counts suffice for the local analytic germ and square-root exponential moment, and RH short-window counts yield holomorphy on the punctured b-plane excluding 1.

The exponential weight limsup gives the exact Taylor radius for nonconstant positive aggregates. Weak logarithmic count models allow radius below 1. Formal moments can be indeterminate on the exact m(m−1) lattice without a suitable tail hypothesis.

At every finite Taylor order there are distinct finite positive weighted multiplicity distributions with the same jet and different maximal multiplicity, although C'(0)=0 forces exclusively simple support. Arbitrarily high multiplicity can be hidden by small weight in approximate compact-range data. An exact limiting aggregate C(b)=o((1-b)^(-1)) as b approaches 1 forces simple support. Finite-N prefix staircases do not authorize differentiation of their limiting profile.
